findings.title: Slots inside a date override skip busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot's date matches a date override and the slot is inside the override window, dateOverrideExist is set and checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at the end. Consequently a fixed or round-robin host who has a calendar event or an accepted Cal booking during their override hours will still be reported available, allowing double-bookings on override days.

findings.title: Working-hours check uses slot start for both start and end
findings.body: Both start and end are computed as slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute(); slotEndTime is never used. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHour.endTime (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before closing) therefore passes the check, so checkIfIsAvailable can approve slots that overrun the host's working hours.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects split shifts and approves days with no working hours
findings.body: The code returns unavailable if workingHours.find(...) finds ANY entry for that weekday outside which the slot falls. With split working hours (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) a 13:00 slot is outside the first entry, so it is incorrectly rejected. Conversely, if no entry includes slotStartTime.day(), find returns undefined and the check passes, so a fixed host with no working hours that day is treated as available for a slot generated by another (round-robin) host — defeating the fixed-host enforcement this PR adds.

findings.title: Dayjs object identity comparison for empty override never matches
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The intended special case for an empty override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable all day) is dead code; an early-morning slot on such a day (e.g. 00:00, where slotEnd is not before start and slotStart is not after end) falls through with dateOverrideExist=true and is returned as available.

findings.title: Slots partially overlapping the end of a date override are accepted
findings.body: A slot is only considered outside the override if its end is at/before the override start or its start is after the override end. A slot starting inside the override but ending after it (e.g. override 14:00-15:00, 60-minute slot at 14:30) satisfies neither condition, so it is accepted even though half the slot lies outside the host's override availability. The same find()-based logic also stops at the first override for the date, so a slot valid under a second override range on the same day can be rejected because it is outside the first.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted overrides that cross midnight are placed on the wrong day or dropped
findings.body: startTime/endTime are derived only from hour()*60+minute() after adding the invitee-organizer offset, discarding any day shift caused by that offset. An override near midnight in the organizer timezone (e.g. 01:00 in UTC+14 viewed by a UTC-10 invitee, shifting to the previous day) is rendered at 01:00-style minutes on the invitee day selected by activeOverrides instead of the shifted day, and if the shifted end passes midnight endTime becomes smaller than startTime so buildSlots discards the range (start >= end). Override slots near midnight will be missing or shown on the wrong date.

findings.title: No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides, and the timezone test cannot detect a shift
findings.body: The stated main fix — date overrides of fixed hosts restricting round-robin events — has no test: every scenario added/used here is a single-user event with hosts: []. The added different-timezone assertion at lines 788-804 re-queries with the exact same UTC startTime/endTime window and expects identical UTC slot times, which passes by construction (slots are returned in UTC) and would not catch an override being applied on the wrong local date or shifted across a day boundary in the invitee timezone.
